transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Owen Li (Redwood CSM), Marta Gomez (Seabright Head of ML), Dinesh Rao (Seabright VP Eng), Evelyn Brooks (Seabright Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Seabright SRE)

Summary:
Quick ops readout focused on usage trends, upcoming pilot capacity needs, cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated, and compliance handoffs for a private VPC pilot. Action items and dates agreed. Redwood to run targeted benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- Last quarter usage and burst patterns (daily 9-11am peaks after new feature launch)
- Cost drivers: long-context reranking and frequent embedding jobs
- Reliability incidents and postmortem follow-up (socket timeouts and cold-starts)
- Pilot scope: private VPC vs Dedicated pool tradeoffs, KMS/HSM, SOC2 evidence
- Next steps and SOW/pricing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: All right, good afternoon everyone thanks for joining. we got about an hour blocked for this ops readout and then a decision forum around next quarter capacity, um so I will hand over to Marta to kick off with usage highlights.
[00:22] Marta: cool thanks Jordan, quick context — we shipped the recommendation feature in feb so our inference calls went up like 3x in fifteen days, usually spiky mornings, and then we saw a lot more long context runs for re-rank. latency has been okay but the cost signal is climbing because of the nvme caching and the repeated embedding jobs.
[00:45] Dinesh: yeah and to add, a lot of the load is coming from batch reranks, not just real-time. we're doing a 2k token rerank job that runs nightly across 10k docs, that spikes and then we also have sustained traffic for chat sessions.
[01:05] Priya: okay noted, thanks. question — are you currently pinning a model version or doing latest? that affects KV cache hit rates.
[01:12] Marta: we pin to a forked open model version, some changes to tokenizer happened so we pinned to keep output stable.
[01:20] Priya: good, that helps. Owen: did we get a sense from Seabright on SLA needs for the pilot?
[01:27] Owen: hey yes, we need 99.9 for core generation endpoints and 99.95 for live customer facing chat, because those are revenue impacting.
[01:37] Jordan: got it. quick reality check — 99.95 is an aggressive bar on hosted unless we commit dedicated capacity with hot warm pairings. Dedicated also helps predictability for cost per token.
[01:50] Dinesh: yeah we were leaning dedicated for that predictability, but we wanted to understand the delta in unit cost and whether Redwood's autoscale + burst can meet our peak needs.
[02:03] Priya: that's the tradeoff. we can run a dedicated pool that reserves GPUs and we expose autoscale policies; or we can start hosted with a reserved warm-burst guardrail. the dedicated option gives you KV cache locality and less noisy neighbors so latency and tail-percentiles improve.
[02:25] Marta: latency shape — can you remind us what tail p95/p99 look like on the dedicated path vs hosted?
[02:32] Priya: rough numbers from similar accounts — hosted p95 ~ 220ms for 512 tokens, p99 ~ 540ms depending on model and batching; dedicated — p95 ~ 160ms, p99 ~ 310ms. but your rerank 2k token jobs will push those up. also quantizashun profile matters — we saw a weird CPU fallback when quantization mismatch happened on earlier kernels.
[02:58] Samir: quantizashun, haha I — yeah we've seen some oddities. on our infra side we also have strict egress rules and need to route via our transit VPC. is Redwood able to run inside our VPC or do we need a private deployment?
[03:12] Jordan: you have options: Redwood Private (VPC-managed) is the usual path for that, or we can set up a dedicated on our hosted infra with a private peering. private deployment would put the runtime into your network and you manage keys via your KMS/HSM.
[03:27] Evelyn: for compliance we'd prefer that path, but we need to see the exact checklist — like SSO/SAML integrations, audit log retention, and whether the console exposes token-level cost.
[03:36] Owen: we'll share the security checklist. Jordan will attach the redwood-security.pdf and the terraform snippets for the networking playbook.
[03:44] Jordan: yep shared link will be posted in the follow-up notes.
[03:48] Marta: another ask — for our billing team, can you provide a per-route token cost breakdown and an estimate for nightly rerank jobs? we've shared the prompt set in the drive link but need an estimate.
[03:59] Jordan: yes Priya will run the rerank benchmark using your 2k token prompt set and your traffic shape, and then we can provide an amortized cost per run and per 1M tokens.
[04:14] Priya: quick note — we'll simulate 100 concurrent connections to match the real load patterns; that should capture batching behavior.
[04:21] Dinesh: perfect. also can we validate whether prefix/K-V cache will persist across scaled-down pods, because our rerank jobs are long-running and we want to avoid cold misses.
[04:33] Priya: Redwood's runtime supports continuous KV cache and prefix caching; on Dedicated we can pin cache nodes, on hosted we rely on longer lived instances with sticky routing. there are edge cases during aggressive autoscale down to zero where cache evictions happen. we'll call that out in the pilot SOW.
[04:50] Marta: any notable recent incidents from Redwood side? we had some timeout errors last month and our SRE traced them to a sidecar proxy misconfig.
[04:58] Samir: yes the postmortem showed a 503 spike for about 12 minutes post-deploy.
[05:05] Jordan: sorry to hear about that — we logged an internal issue and patched the proxy health checks. Owen can share the incident link. the pattern we saw was a misconfigured readiness probe causing an abrupt eviction during deploy.
[05:18] Owen: I'll add the incident link to the notes.
[05:21] Dinesh: on pricing — how do reserved capacity commits look? we don't want to overcommit but we want headroom for a holiday promo next qtr.
[05:30] Jordan: reserved commits are monthly or annual tiers. we can craft a stepped commit that covers baseline plus a burst pool you pay a lower standby fee for; then you pay per-token for actual usage beyond commit.
[05:43] Marta: any telemetry we can get in console for predicted burn and recommendations? we need to report to finance.
[05:49] Owen: console has token-level cost, per-route breakdown, and prediction widgets. plus Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization settings to reduce unit cost—we can include that in the pilot.
[06:02] Priya: for the bench we're going to measure three configs: hosted default, hosted w/burst, and dedicated 2-GPU pool with pinned cache. we'll produce latency, cost, and tail p99 numbers.
[06:14] Evelyn: for encryption — keys need to be customer-managed via KMS. can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS or a third-party HSM?
[06:22] Jordan: yes AWS KMS is supported, and we have partners for HSM integrations; we'll include the KMS integration notes in the security packet.
[06:30] Marta: ok timeline check — we'd like to decide on pilot by end of March and start early April.
[06:36] Jordan: that's achievable. action owners and dates listed in the notes.
[06:40] Dinesh: question about model rollouts — if you push a new model variant that slightly changes tokenization, can we pin the model per-route during rollout?
[06:49] Priya: yes, per-route pinning and canary split are supported; also you can enable automatic fallback to previous variant if quality regressions exceed thresholds.
[06:58] Marta: great, we'll need the eval harness to run our regression tests. can Redwood share the eval API or the harness template?
[07:05] Priya: yes — we have an eval harness template and a set of integration scripts; we'll share a repo link.
[07:11] Jordan: ok shifting to a quick cost example — your nightly rerank at 10k docs with 2k tokens, rough simple math: that's ~20M tokens per run; at naive hosted rate that could be expensive. Priya will produce an amortized number.
[07:30] Samir: that matches our finance concerns.
[07:34] Dinesh: anything else on reliability? we are sensitive to burst throttles during the promotional week. is there a pre-warm option?
[07:43] Priya: yes pre-warm is available on Dedicated — you can reserve a baseline number of GPUs for days of expected burst. on hosted you can apply burst credits to reduce cold-start incidence.
[07:55] Marta: one more ask — can Redwood share a sample runbook for incident response and who is on-call? we need to integrate with our PagerDuty.
[08:03] Owen: yes will include runbook + expected on-call response times with standard SLAs.
[08:08] Jordan: quick readout of the pilot SOW items: scope — private VPC pilot, two routes (core gen + reranker), dedicated 2 GPU pool for reranks, retention/ML telemetry 30 days, SOC2 artifacts shared. pricing tiers will have a 3-month optional extension discount.
[08:26] Marta: sounds good. Dinesh any blockers?
[08:30] Dinesh: mostly compliance approvals and we need pricing to make a financing ask.
[08:36] Jordan: understood. we'll aim to send SOW and pricing by 3/18.
[08:40] Priya: technical addition — we recommend enabling prefix caching specially for the rerank route, and reusing KV cache nodes to avoid cold misses, but that requires pinned routing.
[08:52] Samir: will that add extra cost?
[08:55] Priya: a small standby fee for pinned nodes but it pays off if you save recompute on large KV loads. we'll show the delta in the bench.
[09:05] Marta: ok last quick — endpoints and throttling: can we set per-route throttles and per-token burst budgets?
[09:12] Jordan: yes per-route QoS is available; you can set hard or soft limits and priorities.
[09:17] Dinesh: good. let's wrap with agreements and next steps.
[09:21] Owen: recap — Redwood to share SOW + pricing (Jordan), Priya to run bench and share numbers (Priya), Seabright to provide compliance POC and infra details (Evelyn, Samir). pilot kickoff scheduled week of 3/29 pending SOW sign.
[09:38] Marta: thanks all. small note, please add the drive link with our prompt sets and test tokens; I posted permissions for redwood@seabright.
[09:45] Jordan: got it, I'll confirm access. thanks everyone.
[09:49] Meeting end.
